item.title: Re: The Flight of the Koalas
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Veralta. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ LBL
- LBL

Wilpena Pound

This might not be as well known a place to people outside Australia. You might want to add a clarifier after?

Sightings of "flying serpents" are to be quickly verified and acted upon.

“acted upon” is slightly vague. Do you want to give a more specific hint so we can understand the anomaly a little better?

The Foundation History Department is mandated to research texts and information

The tense here is a little inconsistent when compared to the previous sentences. I would remove “is mandated to” and simply put “will” to keep with the clinical tone.

to collect pertinent information.

Again, being specific in the conprocs goes a long way. What kind of information should the Foundation look out for? This adds to our understanding of the scp in the long run.

during 2022

Sounds a little off. You would say “during a year”, but not a specific one. Would change to “in 2022”.

two years after severe bushland fires within the region

Missing an “occurred” after “fires”.

Compiled data indicates a severe decline in population density, upwards of nearly 2,000 per week.

Nitpick, but the second part of this sentence doesn’t link to the first. “2,000” refers to the actual number, not the population density.

It is to be noted that the surviving koala population at this point numbered approximately 62,000.

The past tense of “numbered” indicates that the Foundation is writing from a place of the future? Sorry, just wanted to clarify.

Additionally, testimonies from zoos across and outside the continent indicate that their koalas have also disappeared, despite all efforts to contain or track them.

This was slightly confusing to read. Do you just mean “internationally” or “globally”?

Uluru, Wilpena Pound, Black Mountain2, Arnhem Land, and the Grampian National Park.

Again, these might be entirely foreign terms for those not familiar with Australian Geography. You might want to add qualifiers like “near Sydney” or in “New South Wales”.

Heavy rainfall would occur in tandem

Tenses need to be more consistent, I think. You’re switching between present and future perfect tense, which muddies the viewer’s sense of time.

as SCP-5870 continuously occurs.

A little awkward. You mean to say “at the rate SCP-5870 continues to occur”?

The 2020 bushfires had burned 24 percent of the eucalyptus trees, while approximately 60,000 koalas have been recorded as casualties. 84 percent of survivors have severe burns on their paws, while 31 percent had suffered from dehydration and starvation.

I’m not sure this entire section should be under the “Description” section, as it’s additional context for the anomaly, and not about the anomaly itself. You could re-classify this section as your Discovery log.

SCP-5870-1 instances, despite numerous

“being numerous”.

share striking similaries.

“similarities”. And also, similarities to what? Each other?

bullroarers

Second occurrence of a foreign term without additional context.

These were subsequently fed by the entities to arriving SCP-5870-1 instances

This is happening quite fast, making it hard to keep track of who is who. “These” meaning the nuts? “the entities” here refer to the koalas? I would break up the description and add a little more detail for pacing.

After five minutes, they flew at high speeds

Indicate direction?

which would then hold onto them

“hold” => “cling”. Might want to also specify which parts of the snakes they hold onto.

where a large levitating island, referred to as SCP-5870-2, was discovered.

Whoa, whoa. Why wasn’t this noticed before?

It is to be noted that 40 percent of the island's surface is composed of a lake.

I would remove the “It is to be noted” as this is not something particularly noteworthy.

They then reach a small lake, wherein the main dome is located at its center.

This is confusing. Is the small lake located at the center of the dome? Or is the main dome at the center?

Some of the koala groups make their way to the smaller domes, which are not located in the the lake.

I thought they were deposited at the smaller domes first? “the” is repeated.

koalas living onto them

Unclear what you mean here.

as they are spectated by other koalas.

“as” meaning “because” they are spectated? Meaning unclear.

It is notably

“notably” -> “notable”.

dyed white and yellow.

Again, why is this noteworthy?

The koalas enter the dome.

I thought we were already inside the main dome. Best to clarify earlier where the drone footage starts, and where we’re headed.

manipulated in get fleshy materials

Sorry? Is there a typo here?

After it leaves the SCP-5870-2 duplicate at Mount Warning, SCP-5870-3 has collected approximately 5,600 more koalas.

The sentence structure here is convoluted. Meaning unclear.

the Foundation has listed koalas as critically endangered

Ah? Are we in a Broken Masquerade scenario? Why is the Foundation assuring the public?

Overall, I enjoyed this exploration log, though I felt it went on a little too long and didn’t understand the significance of certain events (like the koalas and kangeroos fighting). You might also want to clarify the description to make it clear what we’re seeing, when.

mitigated these through engineering solutions.

“these” refers to? If it’s the flooding, then the tense should be changed.

10 percent of its national budget to it

“it” refers to?

approximately 115.31 million tons

tonnes of what?

35 Small Modular Reactors14.

The footnote should come after the period.

the TIMES magazine

Do you mean “Time Magazine”?

Closely cooperating with aboriginal groups such as Bundjalung, Eora, and Gamilaaray, greenery restoration programs in New South Wales and Queensland have also been successful

The subject of the sentence is not clear – who is the one “closely cooperating”?

Foundation task forces quickly mobilize. Fortunately, most Australians were celebrating the New Year inside their homes.

I don’t see the link between both sentences?

turn over a new leaf

Personally, this is a highly cliqued phrase, though I can’t say much else if it’s officially a part of lore. Consider rephrasing to simply “turn over” or “turn themselves over” to get the same effect.

+ Overall
- Overall

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?

Well, yeah. It was a wild ride. I’m not familiar with Aboriginal culture (like, at all), and seeing these stories come to life was eye-opening. I just hoped to understand their significance a little more. You’ve clearly done our research and included many references to the culture and origin stories. The main issue (if it really is one in the first place) is outsiders like me don’t really see the significance of the minute events / symbols / objects.

I do like the overarching narrative though of nature taking climate change into its own hands. It’s a strong and relevant message. My major concern would be the deemphasis here on the Foundation’s role in the entire article. Basically, we’re just left as bystanders throughout the entire event, right? Which is fine if that’s what you’re going for, but removes any agency and tension from the narrative.

2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?

Yup, as mentioned above, A good amount of detail included. Just needs to be further explained and the description clarified (who, where and when we are).

3. Does it sound too preachy?

Nope. I think the lesson is clear but not overbearing.

4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

Perhaps I don’t understand the lore and beliefs in the first place. You could be more explicit in this regard, for example, providing an actual story or myth at the beginning, besides just the stone carving.

I also wasn’t clear throughout how the aboriginal community fit into the scp. There’s a passing reference to them creating posters to create awareness, but where do they fit into the story? Wouldn’t it be cool if you could show them being facilitators / active defenders of the entities as the anomalies occur. But again, I don’t want to prescribe a cultural stance for them.

Overall, I’m tending towards an up-vote. The writing is mostly clear, as are the notes and themes you seek to hit.

Thanks for sharing this with us!

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: My tale is about an accountant who monitors the budget of SCP containment procedures (especially Euclid SCPs). Euclid SCPs and Safe SCPs in this tale also have drastically reduced budgets to send more funding to Keter and other high priority SCPs (due to an incident that caused the foundation to receive a significant amount of less funding). However, when monitoring one SCP he notices large amounts of money seemingly going down the drain. After his concerns are dismissed by higher-ups, he decides to launch his own (unauthorized) investigation.

item.title: Re: Knock Box (Seeking Greenlighting)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there XR Titan. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I’m mainly confused: what do a black box, pulling items out of it Doraemon-style, video games and a heart attack have to do in common? The concept sounds like a mish-mash of different ideas in order for you to make it sound as cool as possible. When looked at as a whole, however, do you not see how the concept doesn’t have a central theme, message or even effect?

Ideally, you would want to choose one or two main anomalous effects and stick with them, explain them and derive a story from them. If opening a black box causes a heart attack, for example, cool. Why? What causes this upon opening it? Could it be related to what the user finds or sees on the inside? Likewise, if the opening a black box gives you items, cool. What kind of items? Are they related to the user’s childhood memories, e.g.? You see where I’m going with this? Any effect you introduce to the concept should be thematically linked in some way.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply again. All the best!

item.title: Re: SCP Idea in need of GREENLIGHT
item.content:encoded:
Atention grabber is what brings attention to your article, usually the main aspect of it and what makes it unique, or connections to other SCPs, folklore or mythology, connections to real life people and events. In other words, the things that might catch the reader's attention. In your case it could be the connection to the mystery of the Bermuda Triangle.

On a side note, you have a very basic and bare idea. It would be good to flesh out this concept, specifically the part of the narrative. The story you want to tell is more important than just describing the creature. Hope you find a way to get this idea out there!

item.title: Re: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Sand

So the SCP got bored with what it was doing, so it starts a secret magic cult where abuse and torture is a way of life. The cult gives the SCP a more appropriate form than a hat. The cult starts to grow, and the SCP decided to want to create a dystopian world where people are tortured and sacrificed for its own entertainment (too edgy?) An MTF unit has been ordered to find the cult, stop its growth, and neutralize the SCP before that ever happens.

So basically, there's gonna be some explorations logs of what the MTF finds along the way. While they're trying to locate where the cult is, The cult gets stronger and stronger, so MTF has to hurry before the SCP causes major havoc around the world.

This still doesn't really show much on how and why the skip is like this, the narrative seems more focused on showing it being evil and dangerous (which on its own isn't interesting or inherently engaging), rather than expanding on the questions the concept raised and building up to the payoff over the course of the narrative. Along with this, the proposed narrative doesn't give any context as to how the Foundation found out about the cult, or why they decided that they had to kill it, considering they are against killing anomalies if they can avoid it.

+ show block
– hide block

I thought of another story where the SCP actually achieved world domination, and the whole story is gonna revolve around a man that writes in his journal and describes how life was affected after the SCP took over the world. He and the group of strangers that he's stuck with lives in an abandoned bomb shelter to hide from the wraith of the SCP. He and one of the members of the group volunteer to go outside into the apocalyptic environment to scavenge basic necessities to survive, but they get into trouble along the way.

For the most part, this has the same issues as the first proposed narrative. With the addition of the Foundation being out of the picture, considering this would be written from their perspective, it's odd that they're not mentioned at all.- I have trouble believing they would have been wiped out by this, considering they have dealt with end of world scenarios before.

Journal entry narratives can work very well, however they need to be unique in their own way, they need to have something that will make them stand out. Currently this doesn't really show anything inherently new or interesting, which makes it feel a bit un-engaging. Along with this, the narrative shows little to nothing on the skip itself, there's no real context or information to be learnt from this. How would the draft look if there was little to nothing on the skip itself?

Overall, the both proposed narratives don't seem to focus on the skip or the Foundations quarrels with it much, as they seem more focused on depicting blood and gore, with no context behind it. Which (to me) comes off as a bit edgy, and a quick way to keep audience attention, by raising the stakes and/or making the skip more dangerous.

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch

Anomalous-D (AD) is an extradimensional parasite which feeds on the pain, fear, grief or rage of other sentient entities. It became entangled with our reality and assumed human form eventually finding its way into a Foundation D Class assignment after being captured and convicted of a string of sadistic crimes against animals and people. Its position as a D Class brings it into frequent close proximity of various other anomalies. Anomalous D devises novel ways provoke or torture these anomalies undetected so that it can feed off their pain and rage.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

  • Containment procedure
  • Description of Entity
  • Description of how the creature came to be in containment / details of anomalous nature
  • Addenda:
    • Incident report: Containment breach first drawing scrutiny of AD
    • Memo: List of incident reports possibly involving AD
    • Interview: Log of the interview which reveals AD’s status as anomalous.
    • Interview: Log of feeding procedure
    • Memo: Detailing the variability of AD’s appearance
    • Memo: Possible reclassification as Keter / Thaumiel

Hook / Attention Grabber:

Following a major incident, the Foundation has confined it but is not sure that it is completely contained. Still, the possibility that this new anomaly may be used to injure or possibly destroy other anomalies is cannot be ignored.

Additional Notes:

Anomalous D typically resides between dimensions and might encounter various manifestations of other trans-dimensional creatures on its travels. It would not normally be able to feed on these entities as they would either be too powerful or impossible to hold on to. But in this reality it has found itself – quite accidentally – in a situation where the SCP foundation has trapped them and rendered them unable to defend themselves. Its motivation is to feed on their stress while not getting snared itself.

I expect that I’ll need lots of discussion and refinement to get this where I want it to be. This would be my first SCP contribution and I’m not an experienced writer. Additionally, most of what interests me in this concept are its possibilities for world-building and future story-telling. It will be challenging to bring this to life in a way that hooks the reader while also pointing to the other possibilities.

I have to say, I’m a big fan of creative containment, so you've already got me there. I have three main notes for this concept. First, I think you should be more specific as to what the properties of this anomaly are. Do they manifest cells around them and the resources go missing or do they steal the resources and actively build the cells? This isn’t that big of a deal, I just think it should be clear. Second, I would call this Thaumiel instead of Safe. After all the Foundation’s using it to build cells for other SCPs. The third is more of a recommendation for writing. I wouldn’t recommend making this too long of an article. You’re mentioning interviews and tying this into other SCPs and that’s all fine, I just want to make sure you aren’t going to be running on one idea the whole time. Because I like this concept and I think it’d make for an interesting article, but there isn’t much to say about it from what I’m seeing so make sure not to repeat yourself.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Self-Casting Spell
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A thaumaturgical sentient life-form, living deep in syberia, their culture with strong Polish influences left by Sybiraks. (Sybiraks were the Polish people resettled to Syberia.) It explores both the effects of Polish diaspora and the foundation containing a society.

Central Narrative: It starts off with the special containment procedures (the fenced off part of syberia), then there is a description (about how their bodies are made of what is basically sigils, about how they exchange spells that modify them as plasmids). Then it describes their culture, and the addeneum, where it is described how the sybiraks discover them and describe them, and offer them vodka and rabbit's blood, and how their societies get together, learning from each other and “forming a symbiosis”. It ends with the Incident, when they almost had a civil war.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept, I think. Also the ala genetics that arise inside them, and the weird stuff that arises cause of sentient beings being able to trade plasmids.

Additional Notes: Catholic sentient spells, which form tribes. An idea so weird, that it can work. Also their tribe is divided into three groups:
The Ultracatholics, lead by a Fanatical Pariah Priest, who want to make the other groups just as catholic.
The Tolerant, lead by the youngest of the elders, who want to cooperate with The Foundation, and to learn more of the outside world
The Traditionalists, lead by their shaman, who want to be freed and allowed to go back to the old Yakut ways.

Hi! first of all sorry for not seeing that you weren't taking requests.

I think I could do an interesting narrative if I made it an observant creature, it has been around ever since humanity has been around, and it has observed us since then, it showed a fascination for us as species and showed a wish to be like us, since it hadn't a sense of self it tried to mimic us, but being around for so long it observed humans go all over around the place in customs, beliefs, mannerisms and general behavior, but one thing that is common between humans is the expression through art, so it took that as a landmark, humans always found a need to do art, of course there were different kinds of art but it was always art, so it tried to copy us thourhgt the years and believed that replicating our art is the way to comprehend what is "being human" so it currently is in this endless loop it tries to make art, art regarding every single period he can. but still he can't be like humans, he see us and our actions and it is clear to him that we just operate differently, his art also doesn't erradiate that magic, that soul he sees in human art. so he belives he is simply bad at art, and he keeps trying and trying to get better he tries to make art with crayons to gallons of paint and he still never got that spark, I think the narrative of the article could revolve around the scientist breaking it's current delusional state of existence where he is so deep in the whole "Mimicing humans" thing it thinks each one of its forms are actual people with actual life historys, and after that facade is broken they could get him psychological assistance.

I should also mention that without reading SCP-4576 (which I really need to now!), it was hard to follow along, especially when it off-handedly introduce characters that the reader has never actually met. But regardless of that, it was otherwise super imaginative! The prose really felt tied to the perspective. Solid work from this gift!

Porting my review from the Thread here. I'm still under the assumption that this doesn't really substantiate itself alone, with the introduction of the random characters being really odd and confusing for someone who hasn't read the base scp article yet, but regardless. A neat little thing, but also some work on the prose and wording. Tentative +1

Sorry, sorry, I just remembered the initials GM and thought "George? George sounds right." Alright, so, I have a bit more to spill here.

I put my insecurities in a box so that they take up less forum space!
woot

I was gonna do it in an edit to the author post but… nah. So, you may remember that I got you for a previous Art Exchange as well. I wasn't going to gift to you again except Elogee FishTruck and each did one half of the gifter/giftee organization and he forgot that I'd gifted to you so recently. Not a dig at him at all, just not something I would have done, and it was too close to giving people the PMs as to who they were gifting to change things around, so it went through.

But I see it as an opportunity, because there's some stuff I'd like to say, to my writing acquaintance Conwell. When last I gave you a present, it was rather self-serving, as it was 10,000 words of establishing my own GoI, WWS, in the Those Twisted Pines canon. While I do think you liked On the Radar, it launched into some rather unfortunate, and I believe kind of selfish moves on my part. See, I thought that putting WWS in your canon would have been cool and collaborative. And it would have been!

If you liked it.

And, as it turned out, you ended up rather lukewarm on the WWS tale series that I was setting in the Pacific Northwest. The 16 tales I tagged with your canon, the Stories My Dad Told Me tales, were barely relevant to anything in the canon, except that near the end the intersection with Site-64 and connection to On the Radar became clear. And now, they take up a very eyecatching amount of space on your canon's hub.

An amount of space that makes me the second-largest Twisted Pines contributor in terms of article count, and yet I had barely read any of it when I started writing for it. That has been largely remedied now, as I read the majority of the Anderson Robotics arc via researching for this gift, which I kind of see as "making it up to you". And, using this as a way to open the door for conversation… would you rather I remove the twisted-pines tag from the first third of the WWS series and remove them from your hub? If you don't think they're adding anything, which is a possibility I have been quietly expecting for a while, I think it'd be best if I simply removed them. And then this, which more directly ties into everything you've so worked to create, can replace it, and I can be an actual contributor to your canon, not just on a technicality but in spirit.
